topics.label: Introduction and lecture framing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic opens the lecture with framing remarks on the complexity and clinical significance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundations of complement and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental architecture of the complement cascade, its nomenclature conventions, and the central biochemical role of C3 activation.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the upstream recognition pathways that initiate the complement cascade and drive C3 convertase activity on target surfaces.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream effector processes through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and stimulates inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the clinical manifestations and disease phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in various complement pathway components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how microbial pathogens have evolved specialized molecular strategies to circumvent and neutralize complement-mediated immune destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
